text:
Alex P: FYI customer (corp-acme) reports SSO started failing after we rolled out the nginx proxy update. They see a SAML error when returning from the IdP: 'AssertionConsumerService URL not found'. It looks related to a path prefix being inserted by the proxy (/app). Can someone take a look?

Maria G: Can you paste the raw SAMLResponse or at least the ACS URL the SP is seeing? Also what IdP are they using (Okta/Azure/OneLogin)?

Alex P: Okta. Pasting the minimal extracted bits from our logs (sanitized):

```
Incoming SAMLResponse: \n  Issuer: https://company.okta.com
  Destination: https://app.redwood.ai/app/acs\n  AssertionConsumerServiceURL: https://app.redwood.ai/app/acs
  NameID: user@acme.com
  Status: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:status:Requester - "AssertionConsumerService not found"
```

We expect Destination /acs (no /app prefix). Customer says their portal sits under /app and the reverse proxy rewrites path. Previously it worked; proxy change was deployed ~2 days ago.

Jon S: Two likely causes: 1) SP metadata only lists https://app.redwood.ai/acs (no prefixed path) so strict ACS check fails. 2) IdP rotation — if the Assertion signature fails it can show weird ACS errors. But logs show ACS mismatch. Did they recently rotate the IdP cert?

Tara L: I reproduced quickly by running a local Okta SAML test and routing through a proxy that adds /app prefix. Our SP library (python-saml) validates the full ACS URL by default. Repro command I used: `curl -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-urlencode 'SAMLResponse=@saml_response.b64' 'https://app.redwood.ai/app/acs'` results in 400 with same message.

Alex P: Customer sent their IdP metadata URL: https://acme.okta.com/app/acme_sso/sso/saml/metadata. I fetched it and noticed their AssertionConsumerService entries include the full /app/acs. But our SP metadata (internal) only had /acs listed. So mismatch.

Maria G: Two remediation paths: (A) Update our SP metadata for that tenant to include both ACS endpoints (with and without /app prefix) or set ACS index mapping if Okta supports it. (B) Configure proxy to preserve the original request path to the SP (i.e., avoid rewriting the path before forwarding to the application). Which is feasible short-term?

Jon S: Also check entityID in the metadata. I saw a snippet where Okta's SP entityID is `https://app.redwood.ai/app/` while ours is `https://app.redwood.ai/`. That mismatch would also fail metadata-driven checks. We should not alter customer IdP metadata; better to accept both SP-level values.

SupportBot: Ticket #SUP-5421 created and linked to this thread. Priority: P2. Assigned to: Support (Alex P), SRE (Maria G), Security (Jon S).

Tara L: Quick patch I tried: adding an extra ACS endpoint to our SP metadata for the customer's tenant fixed the flow in staging (Okta accepted it). Patch diff: 
```
- <AssertionConsumerService Binding=\"...\" Location=\"https://app.redwood.ai/acs\" index=\"0\"/>
+ <AssertionConsumerService Binding=\"...\" Location=\"https://app.redwood.ai/acs\" index=\"0\"/>
+ <AssertionConsumerService Binding=\"...\" Location=\"https://app.redwood.ai/app/acs\" index=\"1\"/>
```
I also validated signature and everything passed.

Alex P: Customer asked about cert rotation too — they rotated their IdP cert last week. Any chance our metadata fetch didn't pick it up and that's causing intermittent failures?

Jon S: I pulled our IdP metadata cache for their tenant. It showed the old cert and a failed metadata-refresh event around the same time as their proxy rollout. Looks like our metadata fetcher hit a 502 from Okta and didn't retry properly. I triggered a manual refresh and the new cert got pulled in.

Maria G: Action items from SRE side: 1) add better retry/backoff on metadata fetcher + alert if metadata contains unexpected ACS or entityID (so support can be notified automatically). 2) Add a tenant-level SP metadata override UI for adding ACS variants (short term). I'll open infra tickets.

Tara L: Customer workaround while we patch: if they can configure Okta to include our canonical ACS (https://app.redwood.ai/acs) as an additional ACS in their app settings, that'll work. Otherwise we can add the extra ACS on our side for them.

Jon S: Also note — if we start accepting multiple ACS URLs we must ensure we still validate the Assertion AudienceRestriction and enforce RelayState checks. Don't relax signature/issuer validation.

Security Oncall: Confirmed I reloaded the tenant metadata cache and verified the new cert is present. Please test with customer and confirm. I also created a short-term alert: if metadata fetch returns non-2xx three times in a row flag tenant for manual review.

Alex P: I'll send the customer an update with the two workarounds (add canonical ACS in Okta OR we add the extra ACS on our side). I'll ask them to test after we refreshed metadata. I'll update SUP-5421 with the result.

Maria G: Follow-ups (internal): ENG-Runtime - consider logging original X-Forwarded-Path header at debug level for SSO endpoints so we can see when proxies rewrite. ENG-Security - validate the metadata fetch retry patch before release.

Jon S: Leaving a note: avoid changing the IdP's metadata; prefer SP-side compatibility. Also avoid turning off strict ACS checks globally. Customer-specific metadata entries are fine.

Alex P: Thanks team. I'll loop back once the customer verifies. :thumbsup:
